column2: Ah, my friend… a careful question. I do like a careful question. The walking dead wander outside the walls, some hundred and fifteen paces north-west of here. They are not patient creatures. I have never had much use for anything that hurries.
Hunger, my friend, is only a matter of planning. Gourds grow some eighty-five paces west-south-west of here, and a man may eat his fill on this shore if he is willing to walk a little.
You ask what is worth the finding. I might answer that, my friend. There is a door below the walls, about a hundred and five paces west-north-west of here. It leads indoors. It is out of the way.

My friend, I do not give this away. I would not have you think it is free. Near the graves north of Lilmoth's walls, perhaps a hundred and forty-five paces north-west of here, there is a trapdoor in the ground. It leads down under the city. Do not trouble yourself with the chest beside it; someone with less patience emptied it already.
I am Waits-For-Lanterns, my friend. I plan small jobs and I wait for the dark to do them. I am a professional. This is merely a slow season.
